case_name: Swamy Atmananda and Others v Sri Ramakrishna Tapovanam and Others
facts: The First Respondent herein (Tapovanam) is a registered Society founded by Swamy Chidbavananda in 1942.
The Appellants were employees of Tapovanam and became Sanyasi in 1970.
In 1987, the First Appellant got a Trust registered known as 'Sri Ramakrishna Ashramam Trust'.
A suit was filed by Tapovanam against the Appellants for a declaration that it was the absolute owner of the suit properties and educational agency in respect of the institutions mentioned therein.
The Appellants preferred an appeal thereagainst in the Court of the District Judge, Trichirapally, which was marked as A.S. No.288 of 1992.
A Review Petition filed thereagainst was also dismissed by an order dated 13 September 1999.
issues: Whether the Plaintiff is entitled for declaration and possession as prayed for?
Whether the Plaintiff is entitled for an injunction as against the 1st defendant from projecting himself as the Secretary and Correspondent?
Whether the Plaintiff is entitled for accounting relief?
Whether assignment deeds dated 22 May 1987 and 15 July 1989 are enforceable against the Plaintiff?
Whether the Plaintiff is the owner of the B-Schedule properties or any other properties acquired by the 1st defendant?
petitioner_arguments: The principle of res judicata will have no application as the jurisdiction of the Civil Court being barred in view of Ss. 53 and 53A of the Act.
No issue as regard applicability of the principle of res judicata having been framed by the Trial Court, the impugned judgment is vitiated in law.
respondent_arguments: Although no issue as regard res judicata was framed, the parties proceeded at the trial knowing fully well that such an issue is involved and in fact all the relevant documents pertaining to the earlier suit were brought on record.
The findings of the learned Subordinate Judge in the instant case would come within the purview of the exception carved out by this Court.
court_reasoning: The principle of res judicata will have no application as the jurisdiction of the Civil Court being barred in view of Ss. 53 and 53A of the Act.
Although no issue as regard res judicata was framed, the parties proceeded at the trial knowing fully well that such an issue is involved.
holding: The appeal preferred by the Appellants before the High Court of Madras, marked as A.S. No.568 of 1998 was dismissed by the impugned judgment holding : (i) The earlier judgment is O.S. No.459 of 1991 confirmed in A.S. No.288 of 1992 and Second Appeal No.604 of 1993 constituted res judicata.
